description: In 1945, an engineer noticed that the chocolate bar in his pocket had melted next to a radar set. That observation gave us the microwave oven.

hero.hook: One melted chocolate bar, and the modern kitchen changes.

blocks.text: In **1945**, in the United States, the engineer **Percy Spencer** was working on radar. One day he noticed that the chocolate bar in his pocket had melted. Body heat was not the cause: the radar waves were.
He tried it with corn kernels: the popcorn burst. The idea of an oven that heats differently was born.

blocks.caption: Radar sets in the Second World War already ran on microwaves

blocks.text: **Microwaves** are electromagnetic waves, from the same family as light and radio, but more “energetic” than most ordinary radio waves. During the war they served mainly in radar, spotting planes and ships.
Spencer understood that they could also shake the water and the fat inside food, and so heat it.

blocks.caption: The first commercial microwave oven stood as tall as a wardrobe

blocks.text: The first commercial model, the **Radarange**, came out around **1947**. It was huge, expensive, and aimed at restaurants and ships. Shrinking it and making it affordable for households took decades.
At first some people worried that the oven would “make food radioactive.” It does not: microwaves heat food, they do not make it radioactive.
Microwaves mostly make water molecules vibrate, and fats and sugars a little. That agitation creates heat **inside** the food, not only at the surface the way a frying pan does.
That is why a thick dish can be scalding on the outside and lukewarm at the center: the waves do not reach infinitely deep.
From the 1970s and 1980s on, the microwave oven moved into millions of kitchens. It changed habits: quick reheating, ready meals, a faster pace of life.
The microwave oven grew out of an accident Percy Spencer noticed beside a radar set. The waves mainly shake the water in food and heat it from the inside.

subject: sciences
subtitle: By accident
title: The discovery of the microwave oven
